Commentary.Commentary: The news has come in that THE HOSTS HAVE DECLARED THEIR INNINGS ON 202/5 and have set a TARGET OF 490 for Pakistan.

Guess Australia have got what they wanted. A break for their bowlers, a decent batting performance at a quick rate and swelling the lead beyond their opposition. One might see Pakistan come out to bat straightaway after the break. Join us back at 1330 IST (0800 GMT) for the final session.

Smith and Khawaja put on a batting display, with a 111-run stand for the third wicket, thereby eliminating Pakistan's chance of a fightback. Then Handscomb came out and had a quickfire 53-run stand with Khawaja who perhaps missed out on his century. Pakistan managed to get 3 wickets from this session, but they conceded 162 runs in 27 overs. Rahat Ali managed to grab two scalps overall while Amir, Yasir and Wahab have one each.

It is the 'D' word which we all are waiting for and it is a 'D' but it is not the Declaration. It is Dinner. Australia have batted and batted positively, taking the lead and target into the record books, should Pakistan chase it down. A paltry 489 it is, as of now.

1 run.

DRINKS BREAK. Really interesting conversation between Shane Warne and Ian Healy on air. Warne feels that Smith should declare around 30 minutes before the break. Now, when you do that, the break is taken early and the players will arrive directly after 40 minutes. That means, Australia get some time in between lights and daylight, which should make life difficult for the batsmen. In response, Healy agrees and says that normally, ODIs start at 2 pm here at the 'Gabba but for this Day-Night Test, it has been made to 1 pm. So what happens is, because of the tall stands, the shadows start to creep in much quicker than usual. So Warne reckons that may be play for another 8 overs and declare with 30 minutes for Dinner. Excellent commentary.

NOT OUT. The decision stays as it is. But that was very, very close. So Smith survives, only by just. Pakistan lose both their reviews. Misbah seems to be in a relaxed mood though, as he shares a joke with Yasir Shah. Meanwhile, the ball had gone to mid-wicket and the batsmen take a single. Leg bye signalled.

... DAY 3, SESSION 2 ...

Australia have a lead of 327 as of now. They played some really atrocious shots in the first half hour of that innings but have now settled into some proper Test match rhythm. They may be looking to add another 100 runs and then declare. Join us at 1050 IST (0520 GMT) for the second session.
A good session for Pakistan. They bowled well. Warner played a loose shot while Renshaw got squared up. The bowling was excellent, with Amir and Rahat bowling very full and swinging the ball.
